messages:
sophia: Ran into a nasty SSE parse + auth-reconnect combo while testing the mobile sampleapp (iOS + Android). Repro rate ~2% on my laptop under quick reconnects.

sophia: Flow: mobile app opens stream -> auth token refresh happens concurrently -> app reconnects immediately -> sometimes the first `data:` line from new conn is merged into previous partial buffer and parsed as one event. Breaks JSON consumers.

raj: is this limited to our node parser? or also in Swift/Java SDKs?

sophia: I see it in node-sdk samples and in Swift sample using URLSession. Android (OkHttp) is slightly better but not immune. Seems systemic: any client that keeps a partial buffer and only emits on blank-line delimiter will suffer.

mei: can you paste a minimal tcpdump or raw capture?

sophia: quick snippet (raw stream):
```
# conn A tail (no trailing blank line)
data: {"seq":101,"part":"a"}

# conn B head (immediate reconnect)
data: {"seq":102,"part":"b"}

# server saw both bytes in order, but our client parser output (bad):
"{\"seq\":101,...}{\"seq\":102,...}" as a single `data` payload
```

raj: ugh. Two orthogonal causes: (1) parser buffer not cleared on socket close/end, (2) auth refresh/reconnect timing means new socket gets data before parser reset. Fixes: on socket `close`/`error` strongly reset parser; and treat a leading `id:`/`event:`/`retry:` line as implicit delimiter.

mei: mobile-specific: URLSession sometimes coalesces bytes on reconnects when the app reuses the TCP stack; OkHttp has a keepAlive reuse too. So we need SDK parity: Swift/Java should implement the same reset-on-close heuristics.

carl: note: proxies (nginx/gcp lb) sometimes buffer and flush differently; I reproduced higher merge rates when proxy buffering was ON. We should document: for streaming endpoints, disable proxy buffering or set `proxy_buffering off` and ensure `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`/flush for each event.

raj: short-term plan: add a small change in all SDK parsers: on transport `close`/`error` -> if partial buffer non-empty then emit a comment pseudo-event `:partial-truncated` + raw partial (so it won't be parsed as JSON) and then reset buffer. Also add a `sse.handlePartial` opt-in config with values `legacy|comment|drop`. Default `legacy` to avoid surprising behavior.

mei: I'll port that to Swift (URLSession stream task) and Android (OkHttp eventsource wrapper). For Swift, recommended snippet: 
```swift
// on stream close
if !buffer.isEmpty {
  delegate?.didReceiveComment(":partial-truncated")
  delegate?.didReceiveComment(buffer)
  buffer.removeAll()
}
```

raj: for node-sdk I suggested parser.reset() on `req.on('close')` + an optional comment emit. Add integration fuzz test that spawns quick auth-refresh (rotate token) while reconnecting.

carl: also consider server-side mitigation: have sampleapp/backend always append a final blank-line and call `socket.flush()` after each event; send a small `:keepalive` comment every 30s. Helps but doesn't solve SIGKILL/crash cases.

sophia: opened a reproducible harness under dev-tools/fuzz/reconnect-mobile-fuzz.sh that toggles proxy buffering and auth refresh. Attaching logs in the issue.

devex-bot: Created issue DEVEX-2522: "sse: partial buffer + auth-refresh reconns -> merged data events across SDKs" (https://tracker.internal/DEVEX-2522)

raj: next steps: (1) land node change behind opt-in flag and add unit+integration tests; (2) port to Swift/Java with same opt-in and tests; (3) docs update: docs/streaming.md add "Immediate reconnects and client crash edge-cases" section; (4) sampleapp: enable comment-mode for demo builds.

mei: will draft Swift patch and small unit tests today, pinging @raj for review. Also add a note in mobile README about proxy config.

carl: releng: backport request for node 1.4.x and 1.3.x since some partners use older sampleapp pins.

raj: agree. I'll prepare a small RFC blurb in the PR explaining why `legacy` default and why `comment` is recommended for demos. Long-term we should consider adding `id` seq numbers server-side so clients can detect merges.

sophia: thanks all. caught this during partner sandbox tests so high priority for demo stability. I'll update the ticket with the fuzz logs and sample tcpdump.
